title: Go: Hello, World!
description: Print output to the console using fmt.Println, fmt.Printf, and fmt.Sprintf.

steps.title: Print Hello, Go!
steps.description: Write a Go program that prints `"Hello, Go!"` to the console using `fmt.Println`.
hints: Import `"fmt"` at the top of your program.
Wrap your string in double quotes.

verification.failureMessage: Make sure you print exactly 'Hello, Go!'.

steps.title: Print Using Variables
steps.description: Declare a variable `message` with value `"Go is fun!"` and print it with `fmt.Println`.
hints: Use `var message string = "Go is fun!"` or `:=` shorthand.

verification.failureMessage: Print the variable so 'Go is fun!' appears in the output.

steps.title: Format with %v
steps.description: Use `fmt.Printf` with the `%v` verb to print `"I am X years old"` where X is an integer variable `age` set to `10`.
hints: `%v` is the default format verb for any value.
Don't forget the newline — `fmt.Printf` doesn't add one automatically.

verification.failureMessage: Print 'I am 10 years old' using fmt.Printf and %v.

steps.title: Print Multiple Values
steps.description: Print `"apple"`, `"banana"`, and `"cherry"` on the same line separated by spaces using `fmt.Println` with multiple arguments.

verification.failureMessage: Print 'apple banana cherry' on one line using fmt.Println with multiple arguments.

steps.title: Format with fmt.Sprintf
steps.description: Use `fmt.Sprintf` to create a formatted string `"Hello, my name is NAME"` and print it with `fmt.Println`.
hints: Assign the result to a variable and pass it to `fmt.Println`.

verification.failureMessage: Use fmt.Sprintf to create a formatted string and print it.
